verdicts.trueWording: Mister Wolfe doesn't lay out breadcrumbs in a trail...but the clues are there.
verdicts.note: Reactor page fetched live (HTTP 200, browser UA). Sentence appears verbatim in the paragraph on Peace's second layer, directly after 'Alden Dennis Weer is one of these [unreliable narrators]'. Both limbs (no breadcrumb trail; clues nonetheless present) on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: if you chase all the details to their roots, you'll find that Eleanor Bold took the married name of Porter
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the live page in the third-layer paragraph. The chase's terminus is stated there: 'Alden Dennis Weer is dead... Weer is buried and done. He's a ghost, haunting himself.' Weer is identified earlier as the narrator, so the 'narrator is dead' limb is supported.

verdicts.trueWording: The evidence for it is buried, but convincing.
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the live page, immediately after 'Alden Dennis Weer is dead', so the antecedent of 'it' is the narrator's death exactly as the claim states.

verdicts.trueWording: This process of translation is referred to as folk etymology, and it is the primary method Latro uses to record his place names.
verdicts.note: Ultan's Library page fetched live (HTTP 200). Verbatim in the Introduction, immediately after the Foreword block quotation, as the claim's page field says.

verdicts.trueWording: The predominant category is folk etymology, followed by the less frequent use of descriptive, associative, and commemorative place names.
verdicts.note: Verbatim as the final paragraph of the 'Toponymy' section, preceded by 'attempt to classify some of Latro's place names in Soldier of the Mist according to Stewart's taxonomy' — the Stewart-taxonomy limb and the ordering of the three lesser categories both hold.

verdicts.trueWording: he records place names that do not match the literal sounds spoken by a Hellene because he is trying to communicate a deeper meaning about a place
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the 'Folk Etymology' section (sentence ends 'based on his understanding of the language'). The claim's 'sounds he heard' renders the page's 'literal sounds spoken by a Hellene'.

verdicts.trueWording: Latro calls Athens Thought because that's what he thinks it means... although his derivation of it is incorrect.
verdicts.note: Verbatim inside the block quotation in the Introduction, introduced on the page as 'Darrell Schweitzer's interview with Mr. Wolfe that appeared in the Spring 1988 edition of Weird Tales'. Every limb — speaker, venue, date, and the incorrect derivation — is on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: In dealing with place names, I have followed the original writer, who sometimes wrote them as he heard them but more often translated them when he understood (or believed he understood) their meanings.
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the Introduction block quotation, cited on the page as 'Soldier of the Mist, 1986, xii; ... the original Tor hardback edition' and introduced via 'we learn in the Foreword to Soldier of the Mist'.

verdicts.trueWording: We agreed with the basic principle that Severian's post-historic vantage point means that all time is vague.
verdicts.note: Verbatim in section 2.2 'Revising my estimate', in the sentence 'Nigel Price and I were chatting... We agreed'. The page says 'all time' without qualification, in a discussion of Urth's history; the claim's gloss 'in the Solar Cycle' narrows rather than exceeds it.

verdicts.trueWording: In this Wolfe goes against the Vancean grain of numbered Aeons known as history by the grubbing wizards of the dying Earth
verdicts.note: Verbatim in section 2.2; the very next words are 'as in the following examples from Rhialto the Marvellous (1984)', followed by the 17th- and 16th-Aeon quotations, so the contrast limb is on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: Recent reading suggests that the range is actually between one thousand and thirty-thousand years, most accurately "many chiliads"
verdicts.note: Verbatim as the whole of section 2.1 'Overview', whose preceding sentence — 'In "Posthistory 101" and Lexicon Urthus I stated that the time from Ymar to Severian was about a chiliad' — supports the 'revises his own estimate' limb.

verdicts.trueWording: Appian the Elder in no way addresses the particular elusive mystery of why the Autarch's name is never written in Severian's narrative
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the live page, in the same sentence that then turns to 'a few minor mysteries' — matching the claim's stated location. Byline on the page: 'By Michael Andre-Driussi, On 27 August 2008', essay written 1992.

verdicts.trueWording: So 22 chapters before we are given his name or his sobriquet, Hildegrin is described as being like a bear.
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the section opening 'The second bear is Hildegrin', which quotes Shadow of the Torturer ch.1 'as if a dove had momentarily commanded an arctother'. Byline: Michael Andre-Driussi, 28 December 2003.

verdicts.trueWording: So begins, with its Proustian echo, the titular novella of Gene Wolfe's The Fifth Head of Cerberus
verdicts.note: Verbatim in the review's first paragraph, immediately after the novella's opening line; the page credits 'reviewed by Robert Borski' (posted 28 August 2001).

verdicts.trueWording: the last sentence of the novella is as chilling as any written in all of science fiction and effectively encapsulates the mindset of all incipient tyrannical figures
verdicts.note: Verbatim at the close of the paragraph on the opening/titular novella ('while "The Fifth Head of Cerberus" opens up the book...'), so both limbs — chilling as any in sf, and the tyrant's mindset — are supported.
